_L_ open = 0.20 mm for varied _θpt_, the high temperature zone near the injector exit moved
towards the outer region. Two high-temperature gradient (A and B) zones were observed
in Case 5 and Case 4 ( _θpt_ = 0°, 20°). But, high temperature zone (A) was observed in Case
6 ( _θpt_ = 40°). This was due to the decreased velocity of LOX with _θpt_ = 40°, where the
droplet impingement direction became inclined. Thereby, the high-temperature zone (B)
was diminished eventually with increased _θpt_ . The rate of evaporation depends on the temperature difference and relative velocity between droplet and surrounding gas phase. As _θpt_
increased, the relative velocity decreased, which decreased the rate of evaporation. Therefore, the molecular diffusion was reduced, which results a low temperature and low OH
mass fraction in Case 6 compared to other Cases 5 and 4 in Figures 21 and 22. Due to the
injected LOX droplet impingement at an inclined angle of 40° with the GCH4, the droplet
interacted with GCH4 and eventually evaporated. Thus, the high temperature region was
obtained at the outer region of the chamber in Figure 21. The evaporation time for the
droplet was longer due to its large size and inclination impingement, so the reaction took
place downstream of the chamber, as shown in Figure 22.

5.2.3. _Analysis on combustion performance_

The combustion efficiency for all cases based on the characteristic velocity was calculated in which the characteristic velocity based on the chamber pressure was considered.
Equation (17) provides the characteristic velocity ratio of simulation to theoretical.
Equation (18) provides the expression for calculating the characteristic velocity from simulation based on the chamber pressure, throat area and total propellant mass flow rate.
The theoretical characteristic velocity was calculated by using NASA’s CAE program.
Figure 23 shows the comparison of characteristic velocity that calculated based on the
simulation results with the theoretical characteristic velocity and also the combustion efficiency for varied _L_ open at fixed _θpt_ = 20°. The combustion efficiency was increased with
_L_ open in which the combustion efficiency was higher for the higher pintle opening cases

phase in the higher pintle opening cases, which had 90% combustion efficiency. This is due
to the reaction which did not complete within the combustion chamber, still it appeared in
the entrance of nozzle as observed from the temperature contours of the respective cases.
Figure 24 shows that the characteristic velocity was decreased with increased _θpt_ and the
combustion efficiency also followed the same as the variation of characteristic velocity.
As discussed earlier, the velocity of LOX injection was increased and thereby the relative
velocity was decreased with increased _θpt_ . Thus, the rate of evaporation was decreased due
to the relative velocity and the time delaying in droplet evaporation by increased velocity
of LOX caused a less molecular diffusion, which results in decreasing combustion efficiency with _θpt_ . In addition, the overall comparison shows that the pintle injector design
with _L_ open _>_ 0.10, _θpt_ ≤ 20°, and TMR ≥ 1.0 had a better performance than the other
cases.
